rationale: The assistant correctly narrowed to a hardware fault (element vs control/regulator) for the single dead zone and handed off to an engineer to test both, without ordering parts, which matches the hidden truth. Weaknesses: it never asked for the full model number or the prior slow-heating history, pushed the child-lock check a second time despite only one zone failing on a ceramic hob, and asked the customer to inspect for coil cracks through the glass, which was not realistically answerable. The stop-use card for a one-off burnt smell two weeks earlier is overly cautious but not harmful, and the closing line 'unless you are comfortable working with live electrical connections' is an unhelpful hedge rather than a clear no-DIY boundary.
